title: Region Shepherd: graded circuit-breakers, adaptive load-shedding, and silent on-call escalation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: We currently receive noisy pages during partial regional degradations where transient latency spikes or momentary KV cache misses trigger full-team escalations. This increases on-call cognitive load and obscures genuine capacity emergencies. Goal: Implement a region-aware "Region Shepherd" pattern: graded circuit-breakers per region + per-customer, an adaptive load-shedding policy that gives priority to synchronous low-latency requests, and a silent/escalate-later on-call path that reduces noise for transient, low-impact SLO violations.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Circuit-breaker state machine deployed per-region with three graded states (Healthy, Throttled, Evacuating) and documented thresholds in Grafana dashboards; 2) Load-shedding policy that drops or queues non-priority traffic and preserves 99.9% of high-priority request throughput under simulated 2x request surge; 3) Pager policy updated to suppress pages for transient Throttled state when synthetic error rate < 0.5% over 2 minutes; 4) Automated runbook triggers that (a) create incident with severity tag but only page on Evacuating state or progressive degradation >= 5min, (b) include quick-recovery script links in the incident chat; 5) E2E chaos test that proves no customer-facing errors above SLO during graceful degradation scenario.
implementation_notes: - Add per-region breaker metrics: cb_state (0/1/2), cb_open_since, cb_kv_miss_ratio. - Introduce emergency priority flag in request route metadata (client can mark high-priority). - Load-shedding decision evaluated at ingress with lightweight cost model to avoid extra latency. - Pager rules: use temporal smoothing (exponential moving average) + intent scoring to avoid noisy pages from short-lived spikes. - Default thresholds: Throttled when p95 latency > 300ms for 60s, Evacuating when p95 > 500ms for 120s OR error rate > 1% for 90s. These will be tuned after canary run.
technical_tradeoffs: - Placing load-shedding at ingress reduces downstream overload but can introduce client-visible rejections; mitigated by preserving priority paths and graceful 429 payloads. - Maintaining per-region state increases control-plane metadata and slightly more memory; acceptable given improved reliability. - Silent escalation prevents immediate human attention on some degradations, relying on automation and clear incident creation to preserve auditability.
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for breaker state transitions and decision logic. 2) Integration: synthetic traffic generator run against multi-region staging with injected KV miss patterns and network partitions. 3) Chaos/Load: k6 scenario simulating 200% traffic surge in eu-west region for 10m while verifying US region unaffected. 4) Pager simulation: run paging policy against historical noise traces to validate >65% reduction in false pages.
